st.2: Bronze was made by alloying copper with zinc.
st.1: The Harappans pioneered the use of silver, which they mined at Khetri in Rajasthan.

x: Only statement 4 is correct: the Dancing Girl was cast by the lost-wax process. Statement 1 is wrong: silver was imported (from Afghanistan/Iran) and Khetri supplied copper. Statement 2 is wrong: bronze is copper + tin (copper + zinc is brass). Statement 3 is wrong: pure copper objects far outnumber bronze ones.

st.4: Tibet is the mainstream and most plausible view.
st.1: Dayananda Saraswati put forward his view in The Arctic Home in the Vedas.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: A.C. Das placed the original home in Sapta Sindhu. Statement 1 is wrong: The Arctic Home in the Vedas is by B.G. Tilak; Dayananda gave his Tibet view in the Satyarth Prakash. Statement 3 is wrong: Ganganath Jha placed it in Brahmarshi Desha (India), Central Asia was Max Muller's view. Statement 4 is wrong: the mainstream view is southern Russia / the Eurasian steppe; Tibet was Dayananda's view.

st.2: All four ashramas are first mentioned in the Rig Veda.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the first three ashramas are referred to in the Chhandogya Upanishad. Statement 2 is wrong: all four are first mentioned in the Jabala Upanishad; the Rig Veda knows no ashramas. Statement 3 is wrong: Brahmacharya came first and Sannyasa was the last to be established.

st.3: A deposit of 2,000 karshapanas was made with a guild of weavers for the monks' robes.

x: All three statements are correct: the Ikshvaku Veerapurushadatta is linked with the Maha Chaitya of Nagarjunakonda, Upasika Bodhisri served under Ehuvala Chantamula, and lay patrons deposited 2,000 karshapanas with a weavers' guild for the monks' robes.

st.2: He renounced the world at 30 and died at 72, about 250 years before Mahavira.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: Parshvanatha was born at Varanasi to Asvasena and Vama. Statement 2 is wrong: he died at 100; 72 was Mahavira's age at death. Statement 3 is wrong: he attained nirvana at Sammed Shikhar (Parasnath hill); Pavapuri is Mahavira's.

st.3: The Orugallu Kaifiyat records the flight of a Jain monk to Hanamkonda from Rajaraja Narendra's persecution.

x: All three statements are correct: Ramatirtham was a Jain hill centre where the Kalyanakaraka was written, Shudras took up Jainism under the Eastern Chalukyas, and the Orugallu Kaifiyat records a Jain monk's flight to Hanamkonda from Rajaraja Narendra's persecution.

st.1: It was fought in c. 261 BCE, the year of Ashoka's coronation.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: Kalinga had broken free in Bindusara's last years. Statement 1 is wrong: the war came in Ashoka's 8th regnal year, not the year of his coronation. Statement 2 is wrong: Rock Edict XIII says about 1,50,000 were deported and 1,00,000 killed.

st.1: Pranaya was the king's regular share of the produce.
st.2: Bhaga was normally one-half of the produce.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Pranaya was an emergency tax; the regular share was Bhaga. Statement 2 is wrong: Bhaga was normally one-sixth (one-fourth in some accounts). Statement 3 is wrong: income from crown land was Sita; Bali was an additional levy or tribute.

st.2: Nalanda was destroyed by Bakhtiyar Khalji.

x: All three statements are correct: Cunningham identified Nalanda in 1861, it was destroyed by Bakhtiyar Khalji, and the Damodarpur copper plates show guilds working as banks.

st.1: Gujarat was noted for indigo and food grains, and Bengal for sugar and rice.

x: All three statements are correct: Gujarat was noted for indigo and food grains and Bengal for sugar and rice, jins-i-kamil were commercial crops, and tobacco, maize and chillies came from the New World through the Portuguese.

st.3: The Diwan-i-Khas of the Red Fort was the hall of private audience.

x: All three statements are correct: the Red Fort was the core of Shahjahanabad, Agra Fort (1565) had Kasim Khan as architect, and the Diwan-i-Khas was the hall of private audience.

st.2: Jayadeva composed the Gita Govinda in Sanskrit at the court of Ballala Sena.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: Raskhan (Sayyid Ibrahim) was a Muslim devotee of Krishna. Statement 1 is wrong: Ekasarana Dharma centred on Krishna (Vishnu), not Rama. Statement 2 is wrong: Jayadeva was at the court of Lakshmana Sena, not Ballala Sena.

st.3: Sena, one of his disciples, was a barber.

x: All three statements are correct: Ramananda had twelve disciples by tradition, Padmavati was one of his women disciples, and Sena was a barber (Kabir was the weaver).

st.1: It opposed widow remarriage.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: the Virashaivas condemned child marriage. Statement 1 is wrong: they promoted widow remarriage. Statement 2 is wrong: they rejected untouchability.

st.3: Their traditions never hardened into separate sects and panths.
st.1: Caste disappeared under their influence.

x: Only statement 4 is correct: Kabir and Nanak criticised the orthodoxy of both faiths. Statement 1 is wrong: caste persisted despite them. Statement 2 is wrong: purdah did not end. Statement 3 is wrong: their traditions later hardened into separate sects and panths.

st.2: At the coronation he took the title 'Chhatrapati'.

x: All three statements are correct: Shivaji was crowned at Raigad in 1674 by Gaga Bhatt, took the title Chhatrapati, and started the Rajyabhisheka Shaka.

st.2: His 1677 alliance with Abul Hasan Tana Shah of Bijapur was arranged through Madanna (Mir Jumla) and Akkanna (Sar Lashkar).
st.4: Shivaji died in 1689.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: in 1677 Shivaji took Gingee and Vellore. Statement 2 is wrong: Abul Hasan Tana Shah was the ruler of Golconda, not Bijapur. Statement 3 is wrong: Shivaji did not share the spoils with Golconda. Statement 4 is wrong: Shivaji died in 1680 (1689 is when Sambhaji was executed).

st.1: Qasim Khan, Aurangzeb's governor of Bengal, took Hooghly from the Portuguese in 1632.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: Portugal's union with Spain (1580) weakened it in India. Statement 1 is wrong: Qasim Khan was Shah Jahan's governor. Statement 2 is wrong: Shaista Khan was Aurangzeb's governor of Bengal.

st.3: Madras became India's first municipal corporation in 1688.

x: All three statements are correct: Francis Day founded Madras with Andrew Cogan, the Damerla brothers helped obtain the grant, and Madras got India's first municipal corporation in 1688.

st.3: Karaikal, settled in 1723, was the only French territorial possession in Andhra.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: Marcara set up the French factory at Machilipatnam in 1669. Statement 2 is wrong: permission came from Abdullah Qutb Shah. Statement 3 is wrong: the French possession in Andhra was Yanam (1723); Karaikal is in Tamil Nadu.

st.2: Khan Bahadur Khan led the Revolt of 1857 at Lucknow.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: Jagdishpur was in Bihar. Statement 2 is wrong: Khan Bahadur Khan led at Bareilly; Lucknow was led by Begum Hazrat Mahal. Statement 3 is wrong: Kunwar Singh led at Jagdishpur.

st.2: Christian missionaries were barred from preaching in Company territory.
st.1: Sati was abolished in 1829 under Lord Dalhousie.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: western education, railways and the telegraph fed fears of conversion. Statement 1 is wrong: Sati was abolished under William Bentinck. Statement 2 is wrong: missionaries preached freely, even under police protection. Statement 4 is wrong: after 1858 the Crown promised non-interference in religion.

st.2: R.C. Majumdar called it the First War of Independence.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: British historians called it the Sepoy Mutiny. Statement 2 is wrong: the First War of Independence label is V.D. Savarkar's; R.C. Majumdar denied it was a national war of independence. Statement 3 is wrong: the feudal-reaction view stresses princes and landlords; the educated middle class kept aloof.

st.3: The 'double government' it set up was ended by the Charter Act of 1833.
st.2: The Board of Control had six commissioners including the Governor-General.

x: Only statement 4 is correct: the Act cut the Governor-General's council to three. Statement 1 is wrong: commercial affairs stayed with the Court of Directors and political affairs went to the Board of Control. Statement 2 is wrong: the six commissioners included the Chancellor of the Exchequer, not the Governor-General. Statement 3 is wrong: double government ended with the Government of India Act, 1858.

st.2: Before the Ganjam famine of 1865-66 ryots had shifted from paddy to cotton during the Crimean War.
st.3: In the Kurnool famine of 1866 Budda Vengalareddy fed the people and later received a gold medal from Lord Ripon.
st.1: The Guntur famine of 1876-78, known as Dokkala or Nandana Karuvu, killed about 40% of Guntur's people.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Guntur famine (Dokkala / Nandana Karuvu) was in 1832-33. Statement 2 is wrong: the shift to cotton came during the American Civil War. Statement 3 is wrong: Vengalareddy's gold medal came from Queen Victoria. Statement 4 is wrong: John Clough's canal relief was in the Great Famine of 1876-78.

st.1: Warren Hastings took police duties away from the zamindars and set up thanas under an Indian daroga.
st.2: Munro's Judicial Commission placed police supervision under the District Judge.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: the Police Act of 1861 followed the Royal Irish Constabulary model. Statement 1 is wrong: it was Cornwallis who set up thanas under a daroga. Statement 2 is wrong: Munro placed police under the Collector. Statement 4 is wrong: the 1902-03 Police Commission was chaired by Andrew Fraser.

st.2: Lord Minto II succeeded Lord Curzon as Viceroy in 1905.

x: All three statements are correct: John Morley was Secretary of State, Minto II succeeded Curzon in 1905, and the reforms aimed to rally the Moderates and win Muslim loyalty.

st.2: The Bengal British India Society (1843) was formed with A.O. Hume and Dwarkanath Tagore.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the Bangabhasha Prakasika Sabha (1836) was formed by associates of Rammohan Roy. Statement 2 is wrong: the Bengal British India Society was formed with George Thompson, not A.O. Hume. Statement 3 is wrong: the British Indian Association's first president was Radhakanta Deb; Debendranath Tagore was its secretary.

st.1: It was founded in 1902 at Dhaka by Pramathanath Mitra with Satish Chandra Basu.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: the Dhaka branch under Pulin Behari Das organised the Barrah dacoity of 1908. Statement 1 is wrong: the Samiti was founded at Calcutta; Dhaka was a later branch. Statement 3 is wrong: Barindra Kumar Ghosh was Aurobindo's younger brother.

st.2: The raid of April 1930 was made under the banner of the Hindustan Socialist Republican Army.
st.3: The raiders fought a battle at the Jaintia Hills.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: Surya Sen was Secretary of the Chittagong District Congress Committee. Statement 2 is wrong: the banner was the Indian Republican Army - Chittagong Branch; the HSRA was Bhagat Singh's group. Statement 3 is wrong: the battle was at the Jalalabad Hills. Statement 4 is wrong: Surya Sen was hanged in 1934.

st.1: It arose because the government raised land revenue by 22% despite a crop failure.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: it was called off when revenue was to be collected only from those able to pay. Statement 1 is wrong: Kheda arose because the yield fell below one-fourth yet revenue was not suspended; the 22% hike belongs to Bardoli (1928). Statement 2 is wrong: the Gujarat Sabha was led by Gandhi as president, with Patel joining him.

st.1: It was announced by British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald.

x: All three statements are correct: Ramsay MacDonald announced the Award, it gave the depressed classes 71 seats with a double vote for 20 years, and the Congress neither accepted nor rejected it.

st.2: The Constituent Assembly was to have 389 members – 93 from British India and 296 from the princely states.
st.4: The Assembly first met on 9 December 1946 under the presidency of Rajendra Prasad, with the League absent.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the Mission rejected a full Pakistan because of its large non-Muslim minorities. Statement 2 is wrong: it was 296 from British India and 93 from the princely states. Statement 3 is wrong: the Muslim League won 73 seats. Statement 4 is wrong: the first sitting was presided over by Sachchidananda Sinha as temporary President; Rajendra Prasad was elected on 11 December.

st.1: On property, Gandhism stands for the abolition of private property while Marxism stands for trusteeship.
st.2: Gandhi described the State as the march of God on earth.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Gandhism stands for trusteeship and Marxism for the abolition of private property. Statement 2 is wrong: Gandhi called the State violence in concentrated form; the 'march of God' is Hegel's phrase. Statement 3 is wrong: Preamble socialism blends Marxism and Gandhism with a Gandhian tilt.

st.1: Pingali Venkayya wrote 'A National Flag for India' in 1921.
st.3: The Ashoka Chakra with 24 spokes, from the Sanchi stupa, replaced the charkha.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: the present flag was adopted on 22 July 1947. Statement 1 is wrong: the book appeared in 1916 (1921 is when he showed a flag to Gandhi at Bezwada). Statement 3 is wrong: the Chakra comes from the Sarnath Lion Capital. Statement 4 is wrong: the ratio is 3 : 2.

st.1: It rested on Article 371D and the AP Regional Committee Order, 1958.
st.4: It was wound up after the 42nd Amendment (1976).

x: Only statement 2 is correct: its first Chairman was K. Achyuta Reddy of Kodangal. Statement 1 is wrong: it rested on Article 371(1); Article 371D came with the 32nd Amendment. Statement 3 is wrong: in 1968 it was extended by five years. Statement 4 is wrong: it was wound up after the 32nd Amendment (1973).

st.2: Ushavadatta deposited money with the weavers' guild of Bharukachchha at 12% interest.
st.3: Ushavadatta (Rishabhadatta) was Nahapana's son.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Ayama was Nahapana's minister (amatya). Statement 2 is wrong: the deposit was with the weavers' guild of Govardhana (Nasik). Statement 3 is wrong: Ushavadatta was Nahapana's son-in-law.

st.3: He is traditionally dated c. 230-250 CE.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: he was Varnasankarya-nirodhaka and the Nasik Prasasti calls him Ekabrahmana. Statement 3 is wrong: he is dated c. 106-130 CE. Statement 4 is wrong: Ayama was Nahapana's minister.

st.1: Golingeswara is the only temple of the group still standing.

x: All three statements are correct: Golingeswara is the only temple still standing, the ASI attributes the group to Gunaga Vijayaditya III, and the Vijayeswara temple has Ganga and Yamuna figures.

st.3: Prola II was killed by the Velanati Chodas.

x: All three statements are correct: Beta I came to Hanamkonda and attacked Kanchi in 1051, Prola II erected a victory pillar at Srisailam, and Prola II was killed by the Velanati Chodas.

st.1: Koru was a Kakatiya cess on dry land.
st.4: Moturpha was a Kakatiya tax on trades and looms.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: Putti Wahindi was a Kakatiya cess on dry land. Statement 1 is wrong: Koru was a cess on wet land. Statement 3 is wrong: Meruka was a Reddi wet-land tax. Statement 4 is wrong: Moturpha was a British tax on trades and looms.

st.1: Rao Jodha founded Jodhpur in 1459.

x: All three statements are correct: Rao Jodha founded Jodhpur in 1459, the Faruqi kingdom of Khandesh had its capital at Burhanpur, and Rana Kumbha built the Kirti Stambha and Kumbhalgarh.

st.1: On 21 September 1687 the traitor Abdur Razzaq Lari opened the Fateh Darwaza.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: Golconda became the 21st Mughal Suba. Statement 1 is wrong: the gate was opened by Abdullah Khan Pani; Abdur Razzaq Lari fought on loyally. Statement 3 is wrong: Tana Shah died at Daulatabad and was buried at Khuldabad.

st.1: In the Raichur-Bidar campaign Krishnadevaraya freed Sultan Ismail Adil Shah from Barid.
st.3: The salt pans at Pedaganjam were exempted from tax.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: he freed the Bahmani Sultan Mahmud Shah (hence Yavanarajya Sthapanacharya). Statement 2 is wrong: Gulbarga was taken in 1523, after the Battle of Raichur (1520). Statement 3 is wrong: the Pedaganjam salt pans were taxed.

st.3: The Madras Swadeshi League sent Nyapati Subbarao and K. Venkataramana Rao to tour Andhra before Bipin Chandra Pal's visit.

x: All three statements are correct: the movement was called the Vandemataram movement (1906-11) in Andhra, G. Subramania Iyer presided over the Madras Beach meeting, and the Swadeshi League's tour came before Pal's visit.

st.2: Vempatapu Satyam and Adibhatla Kailasam were killed at Barikonda on 10 July 1970.

x: All three statements are correct: the struggle was triggered near Parvathipuram on 31 October 1967, Satyam and Kailasam were killed at Barikonda in July 1970, and Panchadhi Krishnamurthy was killed at Jalantra Kota in May 1969.

st.1: His Misra Manjari won the Sahitya Akademi award in 1965.

x: All three statements are correct: Misra Manjari won the Sahitya Akademi award in 1965, Trunakankanamu was his first independent poem, and Bhava Kavitvam drew on Shelley and Keats.

st.2: Mahapadma Nanda's title Sarvakshatrantaka means 'destroyer of all Kshatriyas'.

x: All three statements are correct: Mahapadma founded the first non-Kshatriya dynasty, Sarvakshatrantaka means destroyer of all Kshatriyas (Ekarat means sole sovereign), and the Hathigumpha inscription credits a Nanda king with a canal in Kalinga.

st.3: Takshashila lay between the Indus and the Jhelum, near present-day Rawalpindi.

x: All three statements are correct: Porus ruled between the Jhelum and the Chenab, Massaga was the Assakenoi capital, and Takshashila lay between the Indus and the Jhelum near Rawalpindi.

st.2: Simuka is associated with ending the Kanva dynasty.

x: All three statements are correct: Satakarni I is said to have defeated Pushyamitra, Simuka overthrew the last Kanva, and Vasumitra defeated the Yavanas on the Sindhu.

st.3: The last ruler, Mahalakadeva, was killed in 1305 by Muhammad bin Tughluq's forces.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: Upendra (Krishnaraja), a Rashtrakuta feudatory, founded the dynasty. Statement 2 is wrong: Bhoja moved the capital from Ujjain to Dhara. Statement 3 is wrong: Mahalakadeva was killed by Alauddin Khalji's forces.

st.3: About 78% of the elderly draw a pension and only about 7% depend on others.
st.4: The elderly account for less than 5% of hospitalisation spending.
st.2: Among Union Territories, Delhi topped the Quality of Life for Elderly Index.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the index was prepared at the request of the EAC-PM, not NITI Aayog. Statement 2 is wrong: Chandigarh topped the UTs. Statement 3 is wrong: about 78% have no pension and about 70% depend on others. Statement 4 is wrong: the elderly account for about 30-35% of hospitalisation spending.

st.1: Godparenthood and dharam bhai/behen bonds are examples of ritual (fictive) kinship.

x: All three statements are correct: godparenthood and dharam bhai/behen are ritual (fictive) kin, Radcliffe-Brown described kinship as a system of dynamic relations, and a father-son tie by birth is consanguineal.

st.2: The 2020 Bodo accord created the Bodoland Territorial Region (BTR).

x: All three statements are correct: ABSU was formed in 1967 with Udayachal as the first demand, the 2020 accord created the BTR (the 2003 accord created the BTC), and the NSCN demands Greater Nagalim.

st.1: The proviso to Article 164(1) requiring a Tribal Welfare Minister does not cover Odisha or Jharkhand.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: Articles 330-342A are in Part XVI. Statement 1 is wrong: the proviso covers Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha. Statement 2 is wrong: Scheduled Areas are declared under the Fifth Schedule (Article 244), not Article 339.

st.2: Telangana became India's 29th State on 2 June 2013.
st.1: Sikkim became a full State in 1975 through the 35th Amendment.

x: Only statement 4 is correct: the Vidarbha demand is from Maharashtra. Statement 1 is wrong: Sikkim became a full State through the 36th Amendment (the 35th made it an associate State). Statement 2 is wrong: Telangana was formed on 2 June 2014. Statement 3 is wrong: Bundelkhand covers parts of Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh.

st.2: The framework consisted of the AP Decentralisation and Inclusive Development of All Regions Act, 2022 and the APCRDA (Repeal) Act, 2022.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: Visakhapatnam was proposed as the executive capital. Statement 2 is wrong: both Acts were of 2020. Statement 3 is wrong: both Acts were withdrawn in 2021; Visakhapatnam was declared the capital in January 2023.

st.1: It recorded 1,07,746 suicides.
st.2: Daily wagers formed about 13% of the suicides.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: ADSI 2024 recorded 1,70,746 suicides. Statement 2 is wrong: daily wagers formed about 31%. Statement 3 is wrong: drug-overdose deaths rose by about 50%.

st.2: PM POSHAN (school mid-day meal) was kept outside it.

x: All three statements are correct: it merged Anganwadi Services, POSHAN Abhiyaan and the Scheme for Adolescent Girls in 2021, PM POSHAN stays a separate scheme, and the funding ratio is 90:10 for the NE and Himalayan States and J&K.

st.3: It pays Rs 200 a month to those aged 65-79 and Rs 500 to those aged 80 and above.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: IGNOAPS is run by the Ministry of Rural Development. Statement 2 is wrong: the Centre's share has been frozen at Rs 200 since 2007. Statement 3 is wrong: the Rs 200 band starts at 60, not 65.

st.3: RSBY (2008) gave BPL families a hospitalisation cover of Rs 30,000 and was later subsumed in AB-PMJAY.

x: All three statements are correct: PMJJBY gives Rs 2 lakh life cover for Rs 436, PMSBY gives Rs 2 lakh accident cover for Rs 20, and RSBY gave a Rs 30,000 cover before being subsumed in AB-PMJAY.

st.3: The SEED scheme (2022) has an outlay of Rs 2,000 crore and its portal is run by the Department of Social Justice.
st.1: The Criminal Tribes Act, 1871 was repealed in 1947.
st.4: DNTs are to be counted in Census 2031.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Act was repealed in 1952. Statement 2 is wrong: the Renke Commission (2008) was the first on DNTs. Statement 3 is wrong: SEED's outlay is Rs 200 crore. Statement 4 is wrong: DNTs are to be counted in Census 2027.

st.1: The UN ceasefire ending the first Kashmir war came into effect on 1 January 1948.
st.2: In Siachen, the line beyond point NJ9842 is demarcated on the ground.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the ceasefire took effect on 1 January 1949. Statement 2 is wrong: the line beyond NJ9842 is unmarked. Statement 3 is wrong: the 2003 ceasefire was reaffirmed in February 2021.

st.2: It was fought in the Siachen and NEFA sectors.
st.3: The K. Subrahmanyam Committee (1963) reviewed India's military failure.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the war ran from 20 October to 21 November 1962 and ended in China's unilateral ceasefire. Statement 2 is wrong: it was fought in Aksai Chin and NEFA. Statement 3 is wrong: the review was the Henderson Brooks-Bhagat Report; Subrahmanyam headed the Kargil Review Committee. Statement 4 is wrong: the Dalai Lama got asylum in 1959.

st.1: It was set up in 1966 with its headquarters at Tokyo, and India is a founding member.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the ADB (1966) is headquartered at Manila, though India is a founding member. Statement 2 is wrong: Japan and the USA are the largest shareholders.

st.2: Jeffrey Armstrong received the ICCR Distinguished Indologist Award for 2015.
st.4: A Festival of India was held in China in 1987-88.
st.1: The ICCR was set up in 1950 by Jawaharlal Nehru.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the ICCR was founded by Maulana Abul Kalam Azad. Statement 2 is wrong: Armstrong's award was for 2021. Statement 3 is wrong: the first Festival of India was in the UK (1982). Statement 4 is wrong: the 1987-88 Festival of India was held in the USSR.

st.1: Its principles are consent of the parties, impartiality and no use of force even in self-defence.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct: missions are run by the Department of Peace Operations and CUNPK is at New Delhi. Statement 1 is wrong: force may be used in self-defence and defence of the mandate. Statement 2 is wrong: missions are created and ended by the UN Security Council.

st.3: 'Introduction to the Study of the Law of the Constitution' was written by Ivor Jennings.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: Granville Austin wrote 'Cornerstone of a Nation'. Statement 2 is wrong: 'Modern Constitutions' is by K.C. Wheare. Statement 3 is wrong: the 'Law of the Constitution' is by A.V. Dicey.

st.3: Under Articles 32, 141 and 142, such guidelines bind only until Parliament makes a law on the subject.

x: All three statements are correct: the Verma-led bench held workplace harassment violates equality and life, the guidelines were replaced by the POSH Act, 2013, and such guidelines hold only until Parliament legislates.

st.3: It amended Articles 13 and 368.

x: All three statements are correct: the 24th Amendment answered Golaknath, made Presidential assent mandatory and amended Articles 13 and 368 (Article 31C came with the 25th).

st.1: States must ratify an amendment within a fixed time limit of six months.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: there is no time limit for State ratification. Statement 2 is wrong: State Legislatures cannot initiate amendments; they only ratify.

st.1: India's amendment procedure provides for a referendum on amendments to federal provisions.
st.2: State legislatures can initiate amendment Bills on federal provisions.
st.3: The 129th Amendment Bill, 2024 proposes a new Article 368A on simultaneous elections.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: there is no special body and no referendum. Statement 2 is wrong: State legislatures can only ratify, not initiate. Statement 3 is wrong: the 129th Bill proposes Article 82A. Statement 4 is wrong: the 131st Bill proposed raising the ceiling from 550 to 850.

st.1: India's Parliament consists of the Rajya Sabha and the Lok Sabha only.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: under Article 79 the President is an integral part of Parliament. Statement 1 is wrong: Parliament is the President and the two Houses. Statement 3 is wrong: State Legislative Councils belong to State legislatures.

st.2: They do not extend to ministers or the Attorney-General.
st.1: The uncodified privileges under Article 105(3) were historically those of the US Congress.
st.3: A member is free from arrest in civil cases during a session and for 60 days before and after it.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: they were those of the British House of Commons. Statement 2 is wrong: they extend to ministers and the Attorney-General. Statement 3 is wrong: the period is 40 days. Statement 4 is wrong: Sita Soren (2024) overruled P.V. Narasimha Rao and removed immunity for bribe-taking.

st.3: While presiding, the Deputy Speaker has the same powers as the Speaker, but an appeal lies to the Speaker against his rulings.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: an Opposition Deputy Speaker is only a convention. Statement 1 is wrong: the date of election is fixed by the Speaker. Statement 3 is wrong: no appeal lies to the Speaker against the Deputy Speaker's rulings.

st.2: Members of the financial committees are elected for a term of one year.

x: All three statements are correct: the Estimates Committee has no Rajya Sabha members, members are elected for one year, and Ministers cannot be members.

st.3: The increase of seats under Section 26 is held up because Article 170(3) freezes seat numbers until the first Census after 2026.

x: All three statements are correct: the Assembly's term counts from that of the united State, sitting MLCs were allotted by the Fourth Schedule, and Section 26 is held up by the freeze till the first Census after 2026.

st.1: Under Article 76 he may speak and take part in the proceedings of either House and of a joint sitting, but cannot vote.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: he cannot advise or hold a brief against the Government of India. Statement 1 is wrong: the right to speak in Parliament is under Article 88 (Article 76 creates the office). Statement 3 is wrong: he is not a Cabinet member nor a full-time servant and may practise privately.

st.3: Judicial review of a Speaker's decision is not available before the decision is made.

x: All three statements are correct: the Tenth Schedule was upheld 3:2, Paragraph 7 was struck down for want of ratification, and there is no judicial review before the Speaker decides.

st.3: In Swaraj Abhiyan (2016) the Supreme Court issued guidelines on mob lynching.
st.1: Under a 'curative petition' the court keeps a case open to monitor compliance.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: the Vishaka guidelines filled a legislative vacuum till the POSH Act, 2013. Statement 1 is wrong: keeping a case open is 'continuing mandamus'. Statement 3 is wrong: Swaraj Abhiyan dealt with drought management; mob lynching was Tehseen Poonawalla (2018). Statement 4 is wrong: Hussainara Khatoon concerns speedy trial; pavement dwellers were Olga Tellis.

st.1: GST compensation cess on luxury and sin goods was guaranteed for ten years (2017-27).

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: compensation was guaranteed for five years (2017-22). Statement 2 is wrong: GST 2.0 took effect in September 2025.

st.1: It cannot inquire into a matter after one year from the date of the alleged act.

x: All three statements are correct: the NHRC cannot act after one year, it only seeks a report on the armed forces, and it cannot take up matters pending before an SHRC or another commission.

st.2: The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 obliged every State to set up a Lokayukta within one year.

x: All three statements are correct: Justice Khanwilkar became Lokpal chairperson in February 2024, States had to set up Lokayuktas within one year, and Justice P.C. Ghose was the first Lokpal (March 2019).

st.3: Jan Sunwai refers to the MKSS public hearings held in Rajasthan in the 1990s.

x: All three statements are correct: Citizen Report Cards came from PAC Bengaluru, a social audit is the Gram Sabha's audit of scheme works, and Jan Sunwai were the MKSS hearings in Rajasthan.

st.3: It is set up under the AP Lokayukta and Upa-Lokayukta Act, 1993.
st.2: The Upa-Lokayukta deals with higher functionaries and the Lokayukta with the rest.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: under the 2024 amendment the term is 5 years. Statement 2 is wrong: the Lokayukta handles higher functionaries and the Upa-Lokayukta the rest. Statement 3 is wrong: the Act is of 1983. Statement 4 is wrong: the selection committee is chaired by the Chief Minister.

st.3: Administrative relations are dealt with in Part XI.

x: All three statements are correct: Part XI covers legislative and administrative relations, and Part XII covers financial relations in Articles 268-293.

st.4: That States lack adequate resources for their duties is an argument against greater autonomy.
st.1: The Anandpur Sahib Resolution (1973) of the DMK wanted the Centre limited to defence, foreign affairs, currency and communications.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: the CPI(M) memorandum of West Bengal was presented in 1977. Statement 1 is wrong: the Anandpur Sahib Resolution was the Akali Dal's. Statement 3 is wrong: the Punjab militancy is cited against greater autonomy. Statement 4 is wrong: lack of resources is an argument for greater autonomy.

st.3: The Punchhi Commission, appointed in 2007, submitted its report in 2010 with 273 recommendations.

x: All three statements are correct: the First ARC study team was headed by M.C. Setalvad, the NCRWC (2000) was under M.N. Venkatachaliah, and the Punchhi Commission gave 273 recommendations in 2010.

st.2: The Centre holds one-third of the total votes in it.

x: All three statements are correct: the Council is under Article 279A, the Centre holds one-third of the votes (the States two-thirds), and it is criticised for curtailing States' taxing powers.

st.3: The CPI completed 100 years of its foundation on 26 December 2025.

x: All three statements are correct: Hume founded the INC in 1885 with Bonnerjee as first president, the CPI formally took shape at Kanpur in December 1925, and it completed 100 years on 26 December 2025.

st.2: The right to contest an election is a fundamental right.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the right to vote is a constitutional/statutory right, not a Fundamental Right. Statement 2 is wrong: the right to contest is a statutory right.

st.1: PUCL v Union of India (2013) held VVPAT an indispensable requirement of free and fair elections, to be brought in phases.
st.2: N. Chandrababu Naidu (2019) raised the VVPAT-EVM tally from one to three polling stations per Assembly segment.

x: Only statement 4 is correct: symbol-loading units are sealed for 45 days. Statement 1 is wrong: the VVPAT ruling was Subramanian Swamy v ECI; PUCL (2013) gave NOTA. Statement 2 is wrong: the tally was raised to five polling stations. Statement 3 is wrong: ADR v ECI (2024) rejected a return to paper ballots.

st.3: Kasu Brahmananda Reddy was the Chief Minister when Andhra Pradesh adopted Panchayati Raj.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: Nehru inaugurated Panchayati Raj at Nagaur on 2 October 1959. Statement 2 is wrong: AP adopted it at Shadnagar on 1 November 1959. Statement 3 is wrong: the CM then was N. Sanjiva Reddy.

st.1: Income distance carries the lowest weight among the criteria.
st.4: Andhra Pradesh's share in tax devolution fell from 4.217% to 4.05%.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: contribution to GDP replaced tax effort. Statement 1 is wrong: income distance carries the highest weight. Statement 2 is wrong: demographic performance is now measured by population growth (1971-2011), not TFR. Statement 4 is wrong: AP's share rose from 4.05% to 4.217%.

st.1: Slum improvement and upgradation
st.2: Urban planning including town planning
st.3: Burials and burial grounds

x: None of these is in the Eleventh Schedule; all four are Twelfth Schedule (municipal) subjects. The Eleventh Schedule instead lists items such as fisheries, fuel and fodder, and the public distribution system.

st.3: It gave a practical shape to Article 41 of the Directive Principles.
st.1: It comprises Articles 243 to 243ZG.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Part IX runs from 243 to 243O (243P-243ZG is Part IXA). Statement 2 is wrong: it has 16 Articles. Statement 3 is wrong: it gave shape to Article 40 (village panchayats).

st.3: Anil Chandra Punetha was appointed State Election Commissioner in April 2025.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: SC/ST seats are reserved by population and rotation, with one-third for women. Statement 2 is wrong: the 18 August 2026 decision kept Mandal Parishad Presidents indirectly elected. Statement 3 is wrong: Punetha was appointed in April 2026.

st.4: The 108th Amendment Bill lapsed in 2019.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: the 81st Bill (1996) lapsed, and the 106th Amendment passed on 21 September 2023. Statement 2 is wrong: on 9 March 2010 the 108th Bill was passed by the Rajya Sabha. Statement 4 is wrong: it lapsed in 2014 with the 15th Lok Sabha.

st.1: Not less than one-half of the seats reserved for SCs and STs are reserved for SC/ST women.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: one-third of Chairperson offices are reserved for women. Statement 1 is wrong: the share is one-third, not one-half. Statement 3 is wrong: unlike SC/ST reservation, women's reservation is not tied to the period under Article 334.

st.1: Results are to be judged not by money spent but by the quality of human character evolved.

x: All three statements are correct: results are judged by human character, not money spent; the Panchsheel was in Nehru's foreword to Elwin's book; and its first principle is development along the tribals' own genius.

st.1: As per the AP Socio-Economic Survey 2025-26, its 123 ULBs comprise 30 Municipal Corporations, 76 Municipalities and 17 Nagar Panchayats.
st.4: The AP Municipal Corporations Act, 1994 applies the Madras City Municipal Corporation Act, 1919.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: the nodal department is MA&UD. Statement 1 is wrong: there are 17 Corporations and 30 Nagar Panchayats. Statement 3 is wrong: the Municipalities Act is of 1965. Statement 4 is wrong: the 1994 Act applies the Hyderabad Municipal Corporations Act, 1955.

st.2: Second-generation reforms were confined to trade and exchange-rate liberalisation.
st.1: First-generation reforms cut peak tariffs from about 125% to about 10%.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: peak tariffs fell to about 30%. Statement 2 is wrong: second-generation reforms covered fiscal rules, disinvestment and governance. Statement 3 is wrong: labour, land and power reforms are second-generation.

st.1: Only atomic energy is now reserved for the public sector.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct: defence was opened to private firms in 2001, and disinvestment began in 1991-92 with Rs 2,500 crore. Statement 1 is wrong: railway operations are also reserved. Statement 2 is wrong: the last SSI items were de-reserved in 2015.

st.2: At the Modi-Xi meeting of September 2025 at Beijing, China stressed Panchsheel as the frame for ties.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: the Tribal Panchsheel was drafted with Elwin, and non-interference is a Panchsheel principle. Statement 2 is wrong: the September 2025 meeting was at Tianjin (SCO summit), not Beijing. Statement 4 is wrong: India recognised Tibet as a region of China.

st.2: Nehru's broadcast of 7 September 1950 declared that India would keep away from power blocs.
st.3: The 13th NAM Summit was held at Havana and the 19th at Kampala.
st.1: The Bandung Conference of April 1955 was attended by 25 Afro-Asian countries.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: 29 countries attended Bandung. Statement 2 is wrong: the broadcast was of 7 September 1946. Statement 3 is wrong: the 13th Summit was at Kuala Lumpur (Havana hosted the 14th). Statement 4 is wrong: the 14th was at Havana; Sharm el-Sheikh hosted the 15th.

st.2: The Neeru-Chettu programme for a drought-free AP was launched in 2015.

x: All three statements are correct: the HNSS lifts Krishna flood water from Srisailam to Rayalaseema, Neeru-Chettu was launched in 2015, and groundwater has overtaken canals as AP's main irrigation source.

st.2: The Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor (1,337 km) is funded by JICA.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the National Rail Plan 2030 targets a 45% freight share. Statement 2 is wrong: the Eastern DFC is World Bank-funded. Statement 3 is wrong: the Western DFC is funded by JICA.

st.3: Blue Box support is subject to reduction commitments.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: converting non-tariff barriers into tariffs is tariffication, and Blue Box payments may be based on 85% or less of base production. Statement 3 is wrong: Blue Box support is exempt from reduction commitments (it is Amber Box support that must be reduced).

st.1: The Census records migration by place of birth only.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: about 141.2 million persons migrated during 2001-11. Statement 1 is wrong: the Census records migration by place of birth and by place of last residence. Statement 3 is wrong: Urban-Urban was the largest inter-State female stream by last residence.

st.2: The DBT Mission is located in the Cabinet Secretariat.

x: All three statements are correct: DBT was piloted from 1 January 2013 in 7 schemes and 20 districts, the DBT Mission sits in the Cabinet Secretariat, and about Rs 6.9 lakh crore moved through 327 schemes in 2024-25.

st.2: Amaravati and Tirupati are the HRIDAY cities of the Telugu States.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: HRIDAY covers 12 heritage cities, including Gaya and Puri. Statement 2 is wrong: the Telugu-State HRIDAY cities are Amaravati and Warangal. Statement 4 is wrong: HRIDAY was launched by the Ministry of Urban Development, not Culture.

st.1: SBM-Urban 2.0, aimed at garbage-free cities, was launched on 2 October 2019.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: the Swachh Vayu Survekshan is run by MoEFCC under NCAP. Statement 1 is wrong: SBM-Urban 2.0 was launched on 1 October 2021. Statement 3 is wrong: Lucknow topped the million-plus category in 2026, with Indore second.

st.3: In Q1 2026-27 growth was led by finance, real estate, IT and professional services at 12.1%.

x: All three statements are correct: manufacturing grew 12.5% in 2025-26, Q1 2026-27 saw manufacturing at 9.2% and services at 10.0%, and finance, real estate and professional services led at 12.1%.

st.2: The youth (15-29) unemployment rate was 7.5%.
st.1: Agriculture's share of employment was 55.6%, well above India's 46.1%.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: AP's agriculture share was 45.6%, close to India's 46.1%. Statement 2 is wrong: youth unemployment was 17.5%. Statement 3 is wrong: rural casual labour was 33.8% in AP against 22.5% for India.

st.2: India missed the MDG target of halving extreme poverty.
st.1: Under the MDGs, India's target was to halve poverty from 47.8% in 2000 to 23.9% by 2015.

x: Only statement 4 is correct: national MPI poverty fell from 55.3% to 14.96%. Statement 1 is wrong: the MDG base year was 1990. Statement 2 is wrong: India met the poverty-halving target. Statement 3 is wrong: $3-a-day poverty fell to 5.3% in 2022-23 (2.3% is the updated national figure).

st.1: It was a statutory body that prescribed guidelines for the national plan, including assessment of resources.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the NDC did prescribe plan guidelines but was an extra-constitutional, non-statutory body set up by executive resolution. Statement 2 is wrong: its advice was not binding.

st.3: It gave top priority to basic and heavy industries.

x: All three statements are correct: Feldman and Mahalanobis developed the model independently, it left consumer goods to small and cottage industry, and it gave top priority to basic and heavy industries.

st.3: The LPG reforms kept multinational corporations out of the Indian market.
st.1: Globalisation is an outcome of liberalisation and privatisation, and import substitution is its major feature.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: outsourcing, not import substitution, is globalisation's major feature. Statement 2 is wrong: Navratna status went to 9 PSUs in 1997. Statement 3 is wrong: the LPG reforms opened the door to MNCs.

st.1: India joined the WTO only in 2001.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct: the WTO replaced GATT, and India's average tariff fell from about 125% to about 30%. Statement 1 is wrong: India is a founding member of the WTO (1995); 2001 is when China joined. Statement 2 is wrong: the Mahalanobis model stressed import substitution and heavy industry.

st.3: It follows the Australian dual model, and the idea is linked with the Kelkar Committee.
st.2: It came into force on 1 April 2017.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: GST came through the 101st Amendment (122nd Bill). Statement 2 is wrong: it came into force on 1 July 2017. Statement 3 is wrong: India follows the Canadian dual model. Statement 4 is wrong: Assam was the first State to ratify.

st.2: Fewer than 10% of UPI users still use cash.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: UPI has not replaced cash. Statement 2 is wrong: more than 90% of UPI users still use cash.

st.2: The e-rupee is a liability of the commercial banks that distribute it.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: UPI is a payment system, not money issued by the RBI. Statement 2 is wrong: the e-rupee is money itself and a liability of the RBI.

st.4: Among NBFCs only housing finance companies can access the LAF.
st.2: The MSF began in May 2011 at repo + 200 bps, with borrowing up to 1% of NDTL.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: the MSF is now repo + 25 bps with SLR dip up to 2% of NDTL. Statement 1 is wrong: the LAF was introduced in June 2000. Statement 2 is wrong: the MSF began at repo + 100 bps. Statement 4 is wrong: among NBFCs only standalone Primary Dealers can access the LAF.

st.3: The three external members are appointed by the Central Government for four years and are eligible for reappointment.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the Governor chairs and has a casting vote but no veto. Statement 2 is wrong: the RBI officer is nominated by the RBI's Central Board. Statement 3 is wrong: external members are not eligible for reappointment.

st.2: The share capital of an RRB is held by the Centre, the sponsor bank and the State in the ratio 50 : 35 : 15.

x: All three statements are correct: Prathama Grameen Bank was the first RRB (1975) under the 1976 Act, capital is shared 50 : 35 : 15 by the Centre, sponsor bank and State, and there are now 28 RRBs under NABARD.

st.2: The NCLT replaced the Company Law Board, the BIFR and the AAIFR.

x: All three statements are correct: the NCLT and NCLAT are under Sections 408 and 410, the NCLT replaced the CLB, BIFR and AAIFR (SAT still exists), and there is a bench at Amaravati.

st.3: The Monetary Policy Committee is required to meet at least four times a year.

x: All three statements are correct: Centre and State spending is about 28% of GDP, Union spending about 13.6%, and the MPC must meet at least four times a year (it meets bi-monthly).

st.2: It is a Union levy under Article 276.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Article 276 caps it at Rs 2,500 a year. Statement 2 is wrong: it is a State levy, not a Union levy.

st.1: IGST is levied by the destination State and apportioned.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: IGST is levied by the Centre and apportioned. Statement 2 is wrong: the State share goes to the consuming (destination) State.

st.1: It was presented on 1 February 2026, a Saturday.
st.3: It was billed as a 'Nari Shakti-driven Budget'.

x: Only statement 4 is correct: its three Kartavyas are growth, human capital and inclusion. Statement 1 is wrong: 1 February 2026 was a Sunday. Statement 2 is wrong: it had no big tax cuts. Statement 3 is wrong: it was billed as a 'Yuva Shakti-driven Budget'.

st.4: Interest received on loans given by the Government is a capital receipt.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: revenue receipts neither create liabilities nor reduce assets, and loan recoveries and disinvestment are capital receipts. Statement 3 is wrong: dividends and profits are non-tax revenue. Statement 4 is wrong: interest received is non-tax revenue.

st.3: Tanks were the second-largest source (24.7%).
st.2: Canals were the largest source of net irrigated area (47.3%).

x: Only statement 1 is correct: net irrigated area was 77.9 Mha and gross 120.3 Mha. Statement 2 is wrong: tubewells were the largest source (47.3%). Statement 3 is wrong: canals were second (24.7%). Statement 4 is wrong: tanks irrigated only about 2.8%.

st.4: India ranks second in shrimp output and exports.
st.1: As of January 2026, China is the largest producer of rice, ahead of India.
st.2: India ranks first in the world in wheat and sugarcane.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: India (150.18 MT) overtook China in rice. Statement 2 is wrong: India is second in wheat and sugarcane. Statement 3 is wrong: India is the second-largest fish producer. Statement 4 is wrong: India ranks first in shrimp output and exports.

st.1: Under DBT in fertilisers, the subsidy is paid to fertiliser companies after sales to farmers are recorded.

x: All three statements are correct: fertiliser DBT pays the companies on recorded sales (not farmers' accounts), neem coating slows nitrogen release and checks diversion, and a 500 ml bottle of Nano Urea is meant to replace a 45 kg bag.

st.4: Budget 2026-27 requires all CPSE purchases from MSMEs to be settled on GeM.
st.1: PMMY loans fall into three categories only – Shishu, Kishor and Tarun.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: PMMY loans are collateral-free up to Rs 20 lakh. Statement 1 is wrong: there is a fourth category, Tarun Plus. Statement 3 is wrong: the RBI limit is Rs 20 lakh, which banks may raise to Rs 25 lakh. Statement 4 is wrong: settlement is to be on TReDS, not GeM.

st.1: The CPSE ETF is a method of disinvestment, but the Offer for Sale (OFS) is not.
st.4: Overvaluation of PSU assets and higher dividend income are criticisms of disinvestment.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: 'selling the family silver' means using proceeds to bridge the fiscal deficit. Statement 1 is wrong: OFS is also a disinvestment method. Statement 2 is wrong: the repo is not a disinvestment method. Statement 4 is wrong: the criticisms are undervaluation and loss of dividend income.

st.3: The World Bank's Human Capital Index (2018) was topped by Singapore, as was HCI 2020.

x: All three statements are correct: India was 131st of 148 in the Gender Gap Index 2025 with Iceland first, the index has four sub-indices, and Singapore topped both HCI 2018 and 2020.

st.3: From BRAP 2020 States were placed in categories such as Top Achievers instead of numerical ranks.

x: All three statements are correct: AP and Telangana were joint first in 2016, AP was first in the 2019 ranking, and from BRAP 2020 States were grouped into categories instead of ranked.

st.1: WIPO, established in 1967, is a UN agency headquartered in Vienna with 193 members.
st.4: The Global Talent Competitiveness Index of WIPO is released at the WEF meeting in Davos.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: WIPO publishes the Global Innovation Index with Cornell and INSEAD. Statement 1 is wrong: WIPO is headquartered in Geneva. Statement 3 is wrong: the International IP Index is by the US Chamber of Commerce. Statement 4 is wrong: the GTCI is INSEAD's.

st.4: The report was published by the IMF as a ready reckoner for foreign investors.
st.2: Singapore topped Doing Business 2019 and Doing Business 2020.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: India was 142nd in Doing Business 2015. Statement 2 is wrong: New Zealand topped both years. Statement 3 is wrong: India's worst area in 2020 was enforcing contracts, not getting electricity. Statement 4 is wrong: the report was the World Bank's, not the IMF's.

st.2: ₹5.43 lakh is the per capita GSDP target for 2028-29.

x: All three statements are correct: Swarna Andhra @2047 targets PCI above $42,000, ₹5.43 lakh is the per capita GSDP (not PCI) target for 2028-29, and Sunrise AP Vision 2029 targeted about ₹9.61 lakh.

st.1: Interest payments in the AP budget are an item charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State.

x: All three statements are correct: interest payments are charged (non-votable), the golden rule limits borrowing to capital assets, and the debt-GSDP and interest/revenue ratios signal sustainability.

st.3: The number of holdings in Andhra Pradesh rose from 85.24 lakh to 96.90 lakh.

x: All three statements are correct: AP's average holding fell from 0.94 to 0.86 ha, small and marginal holdings are 86.21% nationally, and AP's holdings rose from 85.24 lakh to 96.90 lakh.

st.2: AP is the largest producer of farmed shrimp in India, mostly Black Tiger (monodon).
st.1: Horticulture is AP's largest and fastest-growing allied sub-sector, growing at 17.69%.
st.4: AP's sericulture belt lies in Srikakulam and Vizianagaram.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: fishing and aquaculture is the largest and fastest-growing allied sub-sector. Statement 2 is wrong: AP's farmed shrimp is mostly Vannamei. Statement 3 is wrong: Chittoor is the top dairy district. Statement 4 is wrong: the sericulture belt is Sri Sathya Sai/Anantapur (Hindupur) and Chittoor.

st.2: India produces all the commercial silks except muga, which is produced only in China.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct: mulberry is about 90-95% of world raw silk, and the NBHM (2020) runs the Sweet Revolution. Statement 1 is wrong: India is the second-largest silk producer after China. Statement 2 is wrong: India is the only country producing all five commercial silks; muga is unique to India (Assam).

st.2: According to APEDB, Andhra Pradesh accounted for 15.8% of India's exports in 2020-21.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: AP's MSME profile shifted to capital-intensive units, and the IIP base is now 2022-23. Statement 2 is wrong: APEDB put AP's share at 5.8%. Statement 4 is wrong: the core index became nine industries by adding iron ore, not cement.

st.3: APSEZ incentives include 50% stamp duty exemption and a 3% interest subsidy.
st.1: Sri City is a multi-product SEZ in Tirupati district on the AP-Karnataka border.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Sri City is on the AP-Tamil Nadu border. Statement 2 is wrong: the Mega Food Park at Mallavalli is in Krishna district. Statement 3 is wrong: the stamp duty exemption is 100%.

st.1: It was issued by G.O.Ms. No. 11 on 11 January 2016 and is valid for ten years.
st.3: Mega retail status needs an investment of ₹500 crore or more, or 5,000 direct jobs.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: it aims to make AP a retail-logistics hub and promote e-commerce. Statement 1 is wrong: the policy is valid for five years. Statement 3 is wrong: mega status needs ₹100 crore or 2,000 direct jobs. Statement 4 is wrong: it applies only to enterprises with turnover of Rs 1 crore or more or 10 or more employees.

st.3: Diesel prices were decontrolled along with petrol on 26 June 2010.
st.4: India imports hydropower from Nepal from projects such as Chukha, Tala and Mangdechhu.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: petrol prices were decontrolled on 26 June 2010. Statement 1 is wrong: HELP brought revenue-sharing, replacing NELP's production-sharing. Statement 3 is wrong: diesel was decontrolled on 19 October 2014. Statement 4 is wrong: Chukha, Tala and Mangdechhu are in Bhutan.

st.3: India's SPRs give about 9.5 days of cover against the IEA norm of 90 days.

x: All three statements are correct: India imports about 85% of its oil and 50% of its gas, its SPRs are at Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru and Padur, and they give about 9.5 days against the IEA norm of 90 days.

st.1: The polluter pays principle was rejected.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: common but differentiated responsibilities was endorsed. Statement 1 is wrong: Rio endorsed the polluter pays principle (Principle 16). Statement 3 is wrong: Rio did not endorse unrestricted resource exploitation.

st.2: Purchase of machinery is a form of physical capital formation.

x: All three statements are correct: skill programmes build human capital, machinery is physical (not human) capital, and irrigation has no direct effect on human capital formation.

st.2: Set up in 1992, it regulated commodity futures markets.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the FMC merged with SEBI in 2015. Statement 2 is wrong: the FMC was set up in 1953 (1992 is SEBI's statutory year).

st.1: Short-period comets come mainly from the Oort Cloud.
st.2: Long-period comets come from the Kuiper Belt.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: Halley's period is about 76 years, next due in 2061. Statement 1 is wrong: short-period comets come from the Kuiper Belt. Statement 2 is wrong: long-period comets come from the Oort Cloud. Statement 4 is wrong: Hale-Bopp is a long-period comet (about 2,500 years).

st.3: One degree of longitude shrinks to zero at the poles.

x: All three statements are correct: a degree of latitude is about 111 km everywhere, a degree of longitude is about 55.5 km at 60°, and it shrinks to zero at the poles.

st.2: Chhattisgarh is one of the States it crosses.

x: All three statements are correct: 82°30'E passes through five States (UP, MP, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, AP), Chhattisgarh is one of them (West Bengal is not), and AP is the last.

st.2: The Himalayas formed as the southward-moving Indian plate squeezed the Tethys sediments, with the main uplift from the Eocene to the Pliocene.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: the Shiwaliks are the youngest chain and show Jura-type folds. Statement 2 is wrong: the Indian plate moved northward. Statement 4 is wrong: the Cuddapah sediments lie in synclinal troughs.

st.1: The C horizon is the topsoil holding most plant roots.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: the R horizon is unweathered bedrock. Statement 1 is wrong: the topsoil with most roots is the A horizon. Statement 3 is wrong: the E horizon is not present in every profile.

st.2: Cirrus clouds may tower up to about 15 km and give thunderstorms, hail and cloudbursts.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: drizzle falls from stratus, and nimbostratus and cumulonimbus bring rain. Statement 2 is wrong: it is cumulonimbus, not cirrus, that towers and gives thunderstorms. Statement 4 is wrong: cumulus are low clouds of vertical development.

st.1: The mT air mass forms over hot deserts such as the Sahara and Arabia and is hot, dry and stable.
st.3: The very cold, very dry mP air mass originates over the Arctic basin and Greenland ice.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the hot desert air mass is cT. Statement 2 is wrong: an air mass over a cold polar ocean is mP. Statement 3 is wrong: the very cold, dry Arctic air mass is cA.

st.2: On 13 April 2026 the IMD forecast the southwest monsoon at 92% of the LPA, i.e. above normal.
st.3: The Long Period Average of the southwest monsoon is 117 cm.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: NOAA declares El Nino at ONI +0.5°C for 5 overlapping seasons. Statement 2 is wrong: 92% of LPA is below normal. Statement 3 is wrong: the LPA is 87 cm. Statement 4 is wrong: Modoki is Japanese for 'similar but different'.

st.1: Freezing of sea water raises the salinity of the water left behind.

x: All three statements are correct: freezing raises the salinity of the remaining water, the Black Sea is less saline due to river inflow, and melting ice lowers salinity.

st.1: The Lesser Himalaya is also called the Himadri.
st.2: The Dhauladhar extends about 300 km from the Jhelum to the upper Beas.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Lesser Himalaya is the Himachal (Himadri is the Greater Himalaya). Statement 2 is wrong: it is the Pir Panjal that runs from the Jhelum to the upper Beas. Statement 3 is wrong: the Mahabharat Lekh continues the Lesser Himalaya.

st.1: Barren Island, in the Lakshadweep group, is India's only confirmed active volcano.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Barren Island is in the Andaman Sea, not Lakshadweep. Statement 2 is wrong: Narcondam is dormant.

st.4: The distribution of south-west monsoon rain in India is governed mainly by latitude.
st.3: Monsoon winds are confined roughly between 60°N and 60°S.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: 'monsoon' comes from the Arabic 'Mausim'. Statement 2 is wrong: monsoons are seasonal (secondary) winds. Statement 3 is wrong: they are confined roughly between 20°N and 20°S. Statement 4 is wrong: their rain is governed mainly by relief.

st.2: The Mahakali is known as the Gandak in India.
st.4: The Kalagarh Dam is on the Gomti.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the Ghaghara rises at the Mapchachungo glacier. Statement 2 is wrong: the Mahakali is the Sharda in India. Statement 3 is wrong: the Arun is the most important Kosi headstream. Statement 4 is wrong: the Kalagarh Dam is on the Ramganga.

st.1: It is formed by the Tunga and the Bhadra, both rising at Brahmagiri in the Western Ghats.
st.4: The Bhima is its biggest tributary.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: it joins the Krishna at Sangameswaram. Statement 1 is wrong: the Tunga and Bhadra rise at Varaha Parvata (Brahmagiri is the Kaveri's source). Statement 2 is wrong: it is a right-bank tributary. Statement 4 is wrong: the Hagari (Vedavathi) is its biggest tributary; the Bhima is a separate Krishna tributary.

st.3: The Rallapadu project in Prakasam is on the Manneru.

x: All three statements are correct: the Tungabhadra Dam at Hosapete is shared by Karnataka, AP and Telangana, the Annamayya dam breached in 2021, and Rallapadu is on the Manneru.

st.1: Among the pre-2022 districts, Visakhapatnam had the highest rainfall and Anantapur the lowest.

x: All three statements are correct: Visakhapatnam had the highest and Anantapur the lowest rainfall, YSR Kadapa had the largest forest area, and Krishna the lowest.

st.4: About 1,700 km of the 7,516 km coastline is prone to cyclones and tsunamis.
st.1: About 29% of India's landmass is prone to moderate-to-very-high intensity earthquakes.
st.2: About 40% of India's land is flood-prone.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: about 59% is earthquake-prone. Statement 2 is wrong: about 12% (40 Mha) is flood-prone. Statement 3 is wrong: about 68% of cultivable area is drought-prone. Statement 4 is wrong: about 5,700 km is cyclone- and tsunami-prone.

st.1: Chile is the world's largest producer of lithium.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct: Bolivia, Argentina and Chile form the Lithium Triangle, and Indonesia produces over half the world's nickel. Statement 1 is wrong: Australia is the largest lithium producer. Statement 2 is wrong: Bolivia has the largest lithium resources.

st.1: Deccan Trap rocks are known for basalt and black cotton soil.

x: All three statements are correct: Deccan Trap rocks give basalt and black cotton soil, they were formed by Cretaceous fissure lava, and they occur in Prakasam, Palnadu and Guntur.

st.2: National Investment and Manufacturing Zones were introduced under the National Manufacturing Policy, 2011.

x: All three statements are correct: the NMP 2011 targeted 25% of GDP from manufacturing, NIMZs were created under it (not the SEZ Act), and NIMZs differ from SEZs in size, governance, exit and tax rules.

st.3: Daocheng Yading in China is the world's highest civilian airport.

x: All three statements are correct: India is the third-largest domestic aviation market, its airports rose from 74 to 164, and Daocheng Yading is the highest civilian airport.

st.2: Penukonda fort is in Sri Sathya Sai district.

x: All three statements are correct: Lepakshi and Penukonda are in Sri Sathya Sai district, and Kondapalli Fort is in NTR district.

st.3: Dahod (Gujarat) topped the first Delta Ranking released on 29 June 2018.

x: All three statements are correct: AP's Aspirational Districts are Alluri Sitharama Raju, Parvathipuram Manyam and YSR Kadapa, delta ranking tracks 49 KPIs in 5 themes, and Dahod topped the first ranking (West Sikkim was second).

st.2: Subsistence activities in such regions usually need less manual labour.
st.1: WPR tends to be lower in several less-developed, hill and tribal states.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: WPR tends to be higher in such states. Statement 2 is wrong: subsistence activities there need more manual labour.

st.1: Migrants from Konaseema to the GCC countries are mostly women working as housemaids.

x: All three statements are correct: Konaseema's GCC migrants are over 70% women housemaids, Anantapur, Kadapa and Chittoor send many to the Gulf, and Srikakulam fishermen migrate seasonally to Gujarat.

st.4: The CPCB issues algal-bloom and coral-bleaching alerts.
st.2: A red tide is a bloom of red seaweed (macroalgae).

x: Only statement 1 is correct: coastal upwelling occurs when winds push surface water offshore. Statement 2 is wrong: a red tide is a bloom of a pigmented dinoflagellate, not seaweed. Statement 3 is wrong: the Gulf of Mexico dead zone is linked to Mississippi run-off. Statement 4 is wrong: these alerts are issued by INCOIS.

st.1: Its most significant cause is sediment run-off from rivers.
st.2: The first global bleaching event, in 1998, came with a strong La Nina.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the main cause is global warming (rising sea temperature, marine heatwaves). Statement 2 is wrong: the 1998 event came with a strong El Nino. Statement 3 is wrong: the fourth event affected about 84% of reefs.

st.1: Bhitarkanika in Odisha is chiefly known for the saltwater crocodile.

x: All three statements are correct: Bhitarkanika is known for the saltwater crocodile and mangroves, the Chambal Sanctuary lies at the Rajasthan-MP-UP tri-point, and Rollapadu protects the Great Indian Bustard and blackbuck.

st.1: The State animal of Andhra Pradesh is the spotted deer.
st.3: The State tree of Andhra Pradesh is the Jammi (Prosopis cineraria).

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: AP's State animal is the blackbuck (spotted deer is Telangana's). Statement 2 is wrong: AP's State bird is the rose-ringed parakeet; the Indian Roller went to Telangana. Statement 3 is wrong: AP's State tree is the neem (Jammi is Telangana's).

st.1: The demographic transition theory was first put forward by Frank Notestein in 1929 and was named and formalised by Warren Thompson in 1945.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: optimum population gives the highest output per head. Statement 1 is wrong: Thompson first put it forward (1929) and Notestein formalised it (1945). Statement 2 is wrong: the optimum population theory is associated with Edwin Cannan and others, not Karl Marx.

st.1: He shared the 1968 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: Khorana was then a US citizen. Statement 1 is wrong: his 1968 Nobel was in Physiology or Medicine. Statement 3 is wrong: it was for interpreting the genetic code; the ribosome structure was Ramakrishnan's 2009 prize.

st.2: Its nodal department is MeitY.
st.1: It was approved by the Union Cabinet on 19 April 2022.

x: Only statement 4 is correct: it targets satellite-based QKD over 2000 km. Statement 1 is wrong: the Cabinet approved it on 19 April 2023. Statement 2 is wrong: its nodal department is DST. Statement 3 is wrong: it targets 50-1000 physical qubits.

st.2: It is chaired by Dr Pawan Kumar Goenka.

x: All three statements are correct: IN-SPACe (2020) is a single-window agency under DoS at Ahmedabad, it is chaired by Dr Pawan Kumar Goenka, and it enabled SSLV technology transfer.

st.3: PNGRB allowed 5% blending at the start, to be scaled up later.

x: All three statements are correct: the project is by NTPC and Gujarat Gas at Kawas, it blends green hydrogen into PNG, and PNGRB allowed 5% at the start (rising towards 20%).

st.4: Radio waves have the shortest wavelength of all.
st.1: In visible light, violet has the longest wavelength and red the shortest.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: infrared has a longer wavelength than red light. Statement 1 is wrong: red is longest and violet shortest. Statement 3 is wrong: X-rays are shorter than ultraviolet. Statement 4 is wrong: gamma rays are the shortest; radio waves are the longest.

st.2: The James Webb Space Telescope observes mainly in the infrared part of the spectrum.

x: All three statements are correct: JWST (25 December 2021) is a NASA-ESA-CSA mission, it observes mainly in infrared, and XPoSat made India the second country with a dedicated X-ray polarimetry satellite.

st.3: Proba-3, an ISRO mission, uses formation flying of two spacecraft to create an artificial solar eclipse for studying the corona.
st.1: The PSLV Orbital Experimental Module (POEM) uses the spent PS3 stage as an orbital laboratory.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: POEM uses the spent PS4 stage. Statement 2 is wrong: TRISHNA is an ISRO-CNES (France) mission. Statement 3 is wrong: Proba-3 is an ESA mission, only launched by ISRO's PSLV.

st.3: Designed for six months, it worked for about three years until contact was lost in 2017.
st.2: LIBS was one of its payloads.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Mangalyaan carried five payloads. Statement 2 is wrong: LIBS was on the Chandrayaan-3 rover; MOM carried the Methane Sensor for Mars. Statement 3 is wrong: it worked for about eight years until contact was lost in 2022.

st.2: The Uttam AESA radar of the Tejas Mk-1A was developed by LRDE.

x: All three statements are correct: over-the-horizon radar bounces HF waves off the ionosphere, the Uttam AESA was developed by LRDE (DRDO), and an AESA steers its beam electronically with a T/R module on every element.

st.4: It requires only critical-infrastructure organisations, not ministries, to name a Chief Information Security Officer (CISO).

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: NCSP 2013 was released by DeitY and aims at a secure, resilient cyberspace. Statement 3 is wrong: it targeted 5 lakh professionals in 5 years. Statement 4 is wrong: every ministry, department and organisation must name a CISO.

st.2: Targeted advertising at children is permitted with parental consent.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: verifiable parental consent is needed for persons below 18. Statement 2 is wrong: targeted advertising at children is barred. Statement 3 is wrong: behavioural monitoring of children is barred.

st.3: It got statutory status under the Atomic Energy (Amendment) Act, 2015.
st.1: It was set up on 15 November 1983 by an executive order under the Atomic Energy Act, 1948.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the executive order was under the Atomic Energy Act, 1962. Statement 2 is wrong: the Nuclear Safety Regulatory Authority Bill was never enacted. Statement 3 is wrong: statutory status came under the SHANTI Act, 2025.

st.2: Only DISCOMs, not open-access or captive users, must buy a prescribed share of renewable power.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct: a prosumer both produces and consumes power, and the 2006 Tariff Policy was revised in 2016. Statement 1 is wrong: RPOs are fixed by the State Electricity Regulatory Commissions. Statement 2 is wrong: open-access and captive users are also covered.

st.4: About 5 GW of gas-based power capacity is described as stranded.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct: IREDA got Navratna status in April 2024, and India's first sovereign green bonds came in January 2023. Statement 1 is wrong: net zero needs over $20 trillion, not $2 trillion. Statement 4 is wrong: about 25 GW of gas capacity is stranded.

st.1: The Discovered Small Fields policy auctions small fields held by private operators.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct: under OALP firms choose blocks year-round from the NDR, and Samudra Manthan gives 50% drilling support capped at ₹675 crore a well. Statement 1 is wrong: DSF auctions small fields of ONGC and OIL. Statement 3 is wrong: Samudra Manthan is open to all OALP block holders.

st.2: BS-I norms were also called "India 2005".
st.1: India's first vehicle emission norms came in 1991 for diesel and 1992 for petrol vehicles.
st.4: India has generally been ahead of Europe in adopting equivalent norms.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the norms came in 1991 for petrol and 1992 for diesel. Statement 2 is wrong: BS-I was called 'India 2000'. Statement 3 is wrong: Euro I came in 1992. Statement 4 is wrong: India has lagged Europe by about five years.

st.1: AP's wind farms are clustered in Rayalaseema – Anantapur and Kurnool.

x: All three statements are correct: AP's wind farms are in Rayalaseema (Anantapur, Kurnool), wind is AP's second renewable source after solar, and Suzlon is its largest wind developer.

st.3: The Haber process is the industrial process that fixes atmospheric nitrogen.

x: All three statements are correct: nitrogenase drives biological fixation, lightning fixes nitrogen that rain brings down as nitrates, and the Haber process fixes nitrogen industrially (the Contact process makes sulphuric acid).

st.2: The Amazon has been valued at about US$2.2–3.4 trillion a year.

x: All three statements are correct: coral reefs are valued at about US$375 billion–9.9 trillion a year, the Amazon at about US$2.2–3.4 trillion, and critics say pricing undervalues cultural and spiritual services.

st.3: The IUCN World Heritage Outlook 2025 rated them 'significant concern'.

x: All three statements are correct: the Western Ghats are one of eight hottest hotspots, a 2012 serial World Heritage Site of 39 areas in seven clusters, and rated 'significant concern' by IUCN in 2025.

st.1: About one-tenth of India's degraded land faces desertification.
st.4: Europe and North America are the worst-hit continents by desertification.
st.3: According to FAO, about two-thirds of the world's soils are degraded.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: about one-fourth of degraded land faces desertification. Statement 2 is wrong: Rajasthan, not Gujarat, has over 23% of desertified land. Statement 3 is wrong: FAO puts degraded soils at about one-third. Statement 4 is wrong: Africa (the Sahel) and Asia are the worst hit.

st.4: Recycling targets rise from 10% in 2025-26 to 50% by 2028-29.
st.2: The Environment (C&D Waste Management) Rules, 2025 took effect on 1 April 2025.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: India generates about 12 million tonnes of C&D waste a year. Statement 2 is wrong: the Rules took effect on 1 April 2026. Statement 3 is wrong: EPR applies to projects of 20,000 sq m and above. Statement 4 is wrong: targets rise from 25% to 100%.

st.1: Green mufflers are four to six rows of dense trees planted along roads to cut noise.

x: All three statements are correct: green mufflers are dense tree belts that cut noise, CPCB's noise network has 70 stations in seven metros, and crackers above 125 dB(AI) at 4 m are banned.

st.1: The Draft National Resource Efficiency Policy, 2019 was prepared by MoEFCC.

x: All three statements are correct: the draft NREP 2019 was prepared by MoEFCC, it proposes a National Resource Efficiency Authority, and EPR covers plastic packaging, e-waste, batteries and tyres.

st.2: Each of the last three decades has been cooler than the decade before it.
st.1: Air bubbles trapped in tree rings give past CO2 and temperature.

x: Neither statement is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the trapped air bubbles that record past CO2 are in ice cores. Statement 2 is wrong: each of the last three decades has been warmer than any decade since 1850.

st.1: It postponed any decision on loss and damage funding to a later COP.
st.3: The WMO launched the MARS methane satellite alert system there.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: COP27 agreed a Mitigation Work Programme. Statement 1 is wrong: COP27 set up loss and damage funding arrangements including a fund. Statement 3 is wrong: MARS was launched by UNEP. Statement 4 is wrong: AWARe is on water, adaptation and resilience.

st.2: It adopted 100 indicators under the Global Goal on Adaptation.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: COP30 called for at least tripling adaptation finance by 2035. Statement 1 is wrong: the Belém 4x pledge is to quadruple sustainable fuels by 2035. Statement 2 is wrong: it adopted 59 GGA indicators.

st.1: NP-NCD was formerly NPCDCS, launched in 2015.
st.4: SDG 3 aims to cut premature deaths from NCDs by one-half.
st.3: NP-NCD funding is shared 75:25 between the Centre and general States (90:10 for NE/hilly States).

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: NPCDCS was launched in 2010. Statement 2 is wrong: screening covers everyone above 30. Statement 3 is wrong: the sharing is 60:40. Statement 4 is wrong: SDG 3.4 aims at a one-third cut.

st.2: Under PM CARES for Children, a child gets a monthly stipend from age 18 and Rs 10 lakh at 21 years.
st.1: PM CARES for Children was launched on 29 May 2020.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: the Lancet estimated about 19 lakh Indian children lost a parent or caregiver. Statement 1 is wrong: the scheme was launched on 29 May 2021. Statement 2 is wrong: the Rs 10 lakh is paid at 23. Statement 4 is wrong: the PMGKP cover was provided by New India Assurance, not LIC.

st.4: Ebola (2014) was the first PHEIC.
st.2: Mpox was declared a PHEIC only once, in 2024.
st.1: COVID-19 was declared a PHEIC on 11 March 2020.

x: None of the statements is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: COVID-19 became a PHEIC on 30 January 2020 (11 March was the pandemic declaration). Statement 2 is wrong: mpox was a PHEIC in 2022 and 2024. Statement 3 is wrong: the 2026 Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak was declared a PHEIC. Statement 4 is wrong: H1N1 (2009) was the first PHEIC.

st.1: 22 carat gold is 75% pure.
st.2: 18 carat gold is 91.6% pure.

x: Only statement 4 is correct: ruby is aluminium oxide coloured by chromium. Statement 1 is wrong: 22 carat is 91.6% pure. Statement 2 is wrong: 18 carat is 75% pure. Statement 3 is wrong: aqua regia is HCl and HNO3 in the ratio 3 : 1.

st.1: Har Gobind Khorana shared the 1968 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with Watson and Crick.
st.3: Venkatraman Ramakrishnan shared the 2009 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with Steitz and Yonath for the structure of the ribosome.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: Khorana made the first synthetic gene. Statement 1 is wrong: Khorana shared it with Holley and Nirenberg (Watson and Crick won in 1962). Statement 3 is wrong: Ramakrishnan's 2009 prize was in Chemistry. Statement 4 is wrong: he was Royal Society President from 2015 to 2020.

st.2: The BRICS Environment Ministers' Meeting at Bharat Mandapam adopted a Joint Statement.

x: All three statements are correct: the DRR Ministers' statement builds on Udaipur and Kazan, the Environment Ministers adopted a Joint Statement (the Jaipur Declaration was the Tourism Ministers'), and the DRR Working Group met at Puri.

st.2: Its theme was "BRICS and Africa: Partnership for Mutually Accelerated Growth, Sustainable Development and Inclusive Multilateralism".
st.1: It was held at Brasilia on 6–7 July 2025.

x: Only statement 4 is correct: it welcomed India's candidacy for COP33. Statement 1 is wrong: the 17th Summit was at Rio de Janeiro. Statement 2 is wrong: that was the 2023 Johannesburg theme; Rio's was on Global South cooperation for inclusive and sustainable governance. Statement 3 is wrong: the 16th summit was at Kazan.

st.2: The Dunkel Draft (1991) was put forward during the Uruguay Round.

x: All three statements are correct: GATT was signed in 1947 and came into force in 1948, the Dunkel Draft came in the Uruguay Round, and the WTO began on 1 January 1995.

st.3: The ITU Council accepted India's bid to host the Plenipotentiary Conference 2026 (PP-26).

x: Only statement 1 is correct: India was re-elected to the UNESCO Executive Board for 2025-29. Statement 2 is wrong: the 2026-28 UNHRC term is India's seventh. Statement 3 is wrong: India's accepted bid is for PP-30 (2030).

st.3: No founder member holds a veto; the five hold equal shares.

x: All three statements are correct: the NDB was set up under the 2014 Fortaleza Declaration, it is headquartered in Shanghai, and its founders hold equal shares with no veto.

st.2: India and Tanzania became strategic partners in 2023.

x: All three statements are correct: Modi discussed an energy partnership with Venezuela's Delcy Rodríguez, India and Tanzania became strategic partners in 2023, and Dodoma is Tanzania's capital with Zanzibar autonomous.

st.3: Russia's Culture Minister attended WAVES 2025 in Mumbai.
